title: Cedarline Payments — Inference Prioritization & Toolchain Scouting
summary: Intro discovery on model selection tradeoffs for Cedarline Payments. They need multilingual support, long-context for transaction threads (~8k tokens target), tool-calling for payment APIs and retrieval, and strict security (SOC2, KMS). Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC) options and next steps around benchmarks and security review.
topics: context length requirements (8k target, potential 32k for retention)
open model comparison (LLaMA variants, Mistral, Falcon, Emerald?)
tool-calling / function calling for payments workflows
security controls: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-18
Start time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Jon (Redwood SE), Priya (Cedarline Head of ML), Owen (CTO), Sana (Platform Eng), Lucas (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to understand Cedarline's inference needs for payments assistant (multilingual, long context, tool-calling). Focus on hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments and initial benchmarking asks.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya (Cedarline): Hi Priya here. Head of ML.
[00:08] Owen (CTO): Owen — CTO.
[00:10] Sana (Platform): Sana, platform.
[00:12] Lucas (Security): Lucas from security.
[00:14] Maya: Great, from Redwood we have Diego and Jon who will dig into perf and ops questions. High level, we just wanna understand your constraints and what success looks like. Priya, can you kick off with the use case?
[00:27] Priya: Sure thanks. So Cedarline is building an assistant that helps merchants and support agents with transaction investigations. It needs to ingest conversation threads, payment metadata, and sometimes PDFs/invoice snippets. Two main flows: agent assist (low latency, short prompts) and post-transaction summarization / dispute triage (longer context).
[00:45] Priya: For context length we are targeting around 8,000 tokens for typical threads, but some cases go up to ~20k when you include attachments and conversation history. We're evaluating whether 8k covers 90% of traffic or we need a 32k-ish model for edge cases.
[01:05] Maya: Good, that helps. Are you leaning toward hosted API first or do you anticipate Dedicated or Private from day one because of compliance?
[01:13] Owen: Compliance is important. We are SOC2 and PCI-adjacent; we do not store card data in LLM requests, but logs may include identifiers that need to be redacted. Ideally we start with hosted to move fast, but we might need Dedicated or VPC/private deployment before full rollout depending on the encryption/KMS requirements.
[01:32] Lucas: To be explicit, we want customer-managed KMS and SSO/SAML integration, plus audit logs with token-level retention controls. If that isn't available in hosted, that pushes us to private or dedicated.
[01:45] Diego (Redwood SE): Understood. Hosted supports envelope encryption today and configurable retention, but for customer-managed keys and full VPC controls Dedicated or Private is the right path. We can scope a Dedicated pool with private networking and KMS tie-ins.
[01:58] Priya: Cool. On the model side, we're exploring open models to reduce cost and avoid API lock-in — e.g., LLaMA-2 variants, Mistral, Falcon. Need good performance for instruction-following and reliable tool-calling for our payments APIs. Any recommendations?
[02:15] Jon (Redwood SE): For a balance of quality and cost, newer open models on 7B-13B quantized variants look good for short-form agent assist. For the long-context summarization you may want to eval 30B+ or specialized long-context variants. Also consider model variants with native function-calling or clear 0-shot tool interface. We have profiling across Madeira? (misrecognized) — sorry, our catalog lists verified performance profiles.
[02:40] Priya: Right, and multilingual? We need English, Spanish, Portuguese at minimum and ideally code-switching in chat. Some models degrade in pt-br.
[02:52] Diego: Yep, multilingual varies a lot. Mistral community builds and some Falcon flavors have stronger Latin languages if fine-tuned. We usually recommend an eval matrix per language with your sample prompts. We can run multilang evals in the POC.
[03:07] Owen: Latency vs cost is the other tradeoff. For agent assist we need 200-400ms token latency target; for batch summarization throughput matters more. Do you support batching + KV/prefix caching?
[03:20] Diego: Absolutely. The runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache reuse. For agent assist we can pin a low-latency SLO by using smaller model variants or dedicated capacity to avoid cold contention. For summarization we recommend batching and larger sequence-optimized kernels.
[03:35] Priya: You mentioned KV cache — we have long threads; if we can store embeddings or partial KV per session that would help. How persistent is that cache across requests?
[03:46] Jon: We support prefix/KV caching with configurable TTLs; it's not a long-term store but can hold session KV for active lanes. For long-term memory we recommend a retrieval layer backed by your vector DB and function-calling to fetch context at request time.
[04:05] Sana: About tool-calling — our payments APIs require strict idempotency and audit trails. Do you support function calling that returns structured responses and logs for audit?
[04:16] Diego: We have function/tool calling support with structured JSON outputs. You can also route calls through a proxy so your audit log captures every outbound call. The runtime preserves trace IDs for request-level observability. A note though — some open models are noisier in generating structured JSON, so we often add a schema-based post-check or use a small deterministic verifier model.
[04:38] Priya: Good to know. For PII we plan to do client-side redaction before sending, but we need server-side guarantees too. Can we do token-level masking or auto-redaction?
[04:49] Lucas: Also, retention windows: we need logs for 6 months but access paths for audits only for certain roles. RBAC is important.
[05:00] Maya: Redwood's Private can integrate with your KMS, and retention/audit controls are plumbed through the console. RBAC and SSO for login and role-based access to transcripts are supported in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has configurable retention and export but not customer-managed KMS by default.
[05:18] Owen: Sounds fine. On the open model question — how do you help pick model families? Is there an eval you run or do we run our own?
[05:27] Jon: We recommend a two-step: 1) Redwood runs a canned benchmark across 6-8 candidate models for latency/cost/quality with a subset of your prompts (we can run this quickly), 2) You run a larger eval with your full dataset in the POC. We provide tooling and result dashboards.
[05:43] Priya: For quality metrics we care about hallucination in payment facts (amounts, dates), compliance with refusal policies, and deterministic tool invocation. Can you measure hallucination?
[05:52] Diego: We can set eval suites with expected outputs and automated scoring for factual accuracy and generation conformity. For tool-calling determinism we check JSON schema conformance and run post-call validators.
[06:10] Sana: What's the onboarding path if we choose Dedicated? Time to prod?
[06:16] Maya: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 6-8 weeks for reserved capacity and network setup, shorter if you accept managed networking. Private/VPC can be 8-12 weeks depending on approvals. Hosted is immediate — you can be calling APIs in hours.
[06:31] Owen: Cost ballpark? We need rough numbers to compare with Anthropic/OpenAI.
[06:36] Maya: I'll send a dedicated pricing sheet, but high-level: hosted per-token cost with open models is lower; Dedicated gives predictable monthly commits and lower unit costs at scale. Private has higher fixed onboarding. We'll share rough TCO scenarios.
[06:50] Priya: Can we run a benchmark on a 8k context scenario and include pt-br prompts? That'd help a lot.
[06:58] Jon: Yes — Diego and I will run a throughput and latency sim at 8k tokens across 4 candidate models and include Spanish/Portuguese samples. We'll include memory footprint and expected GPU type.
[07:12] Lucas: Security questions: do you support customer-supplied CA or private networking peering? We have strict firewall policies.
[07:21] Diego: Dedicated and Private support VPC peering and private endpoints. For CA and mTLS we can work with your security team. We'll flag any proxy requirements up front.
[07:33] Priya: One more product nuance — tool-calling will need signed webhook payloads and guaranteed delivery semantics. Can Redwood guarantee retries and idempotency hooks?
[07:43] Jon: We surface retries and delivery metrics. Idempotency keys are supported at the function-call layer; you can require signed payloads at your proxy.
[07:53] Owen: Regarding model updates — how do you handle rollouts? We don't want silent model upgrades.
[07:58] Maya: Rollouts are configurable. You can pin versions, do canary or percentage rollouts, and set automatic fallback policies if quality/regression alerts trigger. We also keep model artifacts versioned in the catalog.
[08:12] Priya: Great. Let's talk specifics about the POC scope. We're thinking a two-week technical POC: multilang eval + 8k throughput benchmark + tool-calling integration test. Does that sound reasonable?
[08:23] Diego: Totally reasonable. For two weeks we'll need: sample logs (anonymized), a small test vector for tool-calls, and a security contact to sign off on network access.
[08:33] Priya: I can get the anonymized logs and tool specs. Lucas will handle the security Qs.
[08:38] Lucas: I'll compile the SOC2 scope and encryption questions and send them over.
[08:44] Maya: Perfect. We'll attach the scope doc and a proposed POC plan in the follow-up.
[08:49] Owen: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:52] Diego: Nothing immediate. We might ask for a short test account for hosted trials while we prep the Dedicated POC.
[08:59] Priya: That would help us iterate quickly.
[09:02] Maya: We'll set up a hosted test key with limited quotas.
[09:06] Jon: Quick note — some open models need custom kernel selection for long-context; if you need 20k+ we'll recommend specific GPU types and quantization profiles. We'll include that in the sim.
[09:18] Priya: For the metrics we'll track: latency (p50/p95), token cost, hallucination rate on payment facts, successful tool-call rate, and language accuracy per language.
[09:29] Diego: Good set. We'll make the benchmark sheet to capture that.
[09:34] Maya: Anything else we missed?
[09:37] Sana: One operational ask — can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route/model? We need to show unit economics to product.
[09:45] Maya: Yes, Console exposes token breakdowns, per-model and per-route dashboards, and we can add a custom report for your billing contact.
[09:52] Owen: Ok let's recap next steps.
[09:55] Priya: Recap: Redwood to send dedicated pricing and POC plan, run 8k sim across candidates (incl pt-br), Cedarline to send logs and security docs, schedule POC kickoff for the week of 6/26.
[10:12] Maya: I'll also include a short note on deployment options and what features require Dedicated/Private versus hosted.
[10:20] Lucas: I'll send the SOC2 and KMS questions by 6/21.
[10:24] Diego: We'll aim to have the sim results by 6/25.
[10:28] Priya: Thanks all. Looking forward to it.
[10:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and the pricing doc.

End of meeting.
